title: Form contract
description: What a screen MUST show, written by the owner — not what the code happens to render. The one artifact in this format whose truth is authored rather than measured: check 5 then keeps the built thing equal to the chosen thing. Lines that do not match the code yet are not errors in the contract; they are the product's TODO list, printed by every build.

entity.description: Whose lifecycle the screen lives against. The state vocabulary is the entity's, computed from the cards that touch it — never declared here, or it would be a duplicate that drifts.

field.description: The machine anchor: a data-field/data-section marker the rendered screen carries. The contract names the anchor; the form inventory proves it.

when.description: Entity states in which the element must be present. Absent = in every state the inventory has for this screen.

calls.description: The operation card this control invokes, or null for local behaviour. Naming a card lets check 5 compare shown_when with the operation's data_transition.from — the measured rule: a control is available exactly in the states its operation departs from.

shown_when_rule.description: Availability that depends on more than the entity state, in words. Check 5 can only verify presence somewhere, not the rule itself — written so the limit is declared, not discovered.

opens.description: The form contract this control opens (a modal, an overlay) — a flat link, not a nested tree: nesting was refuted twice by measurement. The opened form is a contract of its own.

groups.description: How the owner groups the screen by PURPOSE: headers, footers, tables, toolbars — and which elements and controls belong to each. Array order IS the group order; a separate order key would be a duplicate that drifts. Membership is authored, not yet verified: the form inventory records anchors flat, so check 5 proves a group's anchor exists but not who sits inside it — a declared limit, like shown_when_rule.

group.description: The container's own data-* anchor (data-section / data-panel-head).

role.description: The group's purpose, not its looks.

contains.description: Fields and controls of this contract, in display order.

removed.description: Controls the owner has decided must NOT exist. Presence anywhere is a finding — a decision is only real while something enforces it.
